title: RDP/SMB/WinRM Abuse
overview: Find repeated administrative sessions between a peer and multiple destinations outside a managed jump-host path.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and windows security or sysmon projection fields.

attack.name: Remote Services
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: Three administrative sessions to distinct targets from a peer source within ten minutes warrant a lateral movement hunt.
evidence: Compare the service, source zone and distinct target IDs. Review authorization and process activity on both sides.
false_positive: An approved desktop-support activity can touch several systems within minutes.
tuning: Maintain separate jump infrastructure and allowlist formally approved tools and accounts by destination class.
response: Verify authorization out of band and scope the account and peer host. Terminate confirmed unauthorized sessions.
prevention: Require segmented management paths, MFA for remote access and monitored privileged accounts.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fields represent a correlated telemetry projection. Individual Windows log types vary by remote service.

questions.prompt: What links the sessions for this rule?
options: A common source IP and distinct targets
questions.explanation: The rule groups the peer and explores lateral fan-out.
